rooms.question: How much of the next row can you predict from three cells?
rooms.ontology: A cellular automaton is a set of states, a neighbourhood, a local update rule and an update schedule.
rooms.action: Select30 or90, lower SPEED, and use RST to restart; predict one next cell from its left,centre,right neighbourhood.
rooms.observable: The same restart recreates a single central seed; different rule presets produce different histories.
rooms.mechanism: _apply_rule forms a3-bit neighbourhood index and reads that bit of the rule integer; _advance writes a fresh row using wrapped neighbours.
rooms.limit: A rule number is a compact truth table, not a ranking from simple to advanced. Changing the display speed changes viewing time rather than the update relation.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Expose the eight neighbourhood cases as visitor-editable switches, preserving the starting row.

rooms.question: What changes when a cell can have neighbours around it in three dimensions?
rooms.ontology: A local rule depends on its neighbourhood and available states; an elementary1D rule is only one possible family.
rooms.action: Observe the growing volume from two sides, identifying occupied clusters and the edges between them.
rooms.observable: A three-dimensional set evolves and stops after20 generations; it carries active and dying-state colours.
rooms.mechanism: StructureGrowth scene overrides rule6-8/6-8/3/M, grid50³,random start,max_generations20. Flexible script counts26 Moore neighbours, applies birth/survival, then a dying state and double-buffer swap.
rooms.limit: Despite this room name, this is a3D multi-state Generations automaton, not a row of elementary Wolfram cases. A stopped display may be its generation cap rather than a stable state.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Place a1D truth-table strip beside one explicit3D neighbourhood to compare what each rule can read.

rooms.question: What happens when the record of time becomes a structure in space?
rooms.ontology: A space-time diagram keeps each successive generation as another row; rendered cells may also become physical supports.
rooms.action: Read from the starting row toward later rows of the bridge, comparing a repeated neighbourhood with the cell it produces.
rooms.observable: Occupied cells become cubes with colliders; absent cells leave gaps in the sequence of rows.
rooms.mechanism: ca_bridge starts with a central cell, advances a1D three-neighbour bit rule and spawns each row alongZ; modulo wraps row ends.
rooms.limit: The bridge currently implements an elementary rule(default30), not Conway B3/S23. A pattern called a bridge does not guarantee a traversable route.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Add a matching B3/S23 dish and explicitly contrast evolving a plane with laying out a row history.

rooms.question: Can one rule support both something that repeats and something that travels?
rooms.ontology: A pattern is a relation among cell states over time, not an extra moving body.
rooms.action: Use the pattern buttons to compare a glider and pulsar; reduce SPEED and watch several generations.
rooms.observable: The glider changes cells while shifting location; the pulsar cycles through shapes near its starting region.
rooms.mechanism: Petri dish applies B3/S23 synchronously with8 wrapped neighbours; patterns are inserted into a64×64 boolean grid.
rooms.limit: The primary remains binary despite the room title. Calling a pattern alive does not give its cells metabolism or intention. Pattern buttons insert and may interact with existing cells.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Compare the binary dish with an explicit third resting state, keeping initial geometry and clock visible.

rooms.question: Does a route remain the same route after somebody occupies it?
rooms.ontology: Here each bridge cell carries a continuous health value; proximity and neighbouring cells update that value.
rooms.action: Approach the bridge from its side, pause near an edge, then withdraw and watch that region.
rooms.observable: Nearby cells lose health and change appearance; away from the visitor they can recover when adjacent cells remain healthy.
rooms.mechanism: Every0.1s local distance<decay_radius decreases health; four-neighbour health>0.5 supports regrowth. Collision turns off below0.2.
rooms.limit: The rule sees proximity to a player-group position, not footsteps, pressure or care. Regrowth requires healthy neighbours; removing all support need not recover.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Compare lingering, quickly passing and returning; record whose presence the player selector uses in a group.

rooms.question: What must remain separate for all cells to share the same present?
rooms.ontology: Double buffering stores an old state and a next state separately so one update cannot read a neighbour already changed during that same step.
rooms.action: Compare the two trays, then trace two neighbouring outputs on the rule90 display back to the preceding row.
rooms.observable: The bench shows separate read/write trays and computed elementary histories alongside other rule-family representations.
rooms.mechanism: _build_elementary starts25 cells, computes each nxt from cur, and swaps only after the whole row. The visible crank and levers are constructed meshes.
rooms.limit: A mechanical-looking crank is not necessarily an operable control. The bench represents the update mechanism; it does not prove every depicted rule-family claim by a live experiment.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Make the crank operable and offer one intentionally sequential update beside synchronous update, keeping the seed identical.

rooms.question: Can similar patterns come from different ways of building them?
rooms.ontology: A resemblance between shapes does not imply the same computation: local temporal updates and recursive spatial copying can share structure.
rooms.action: Select90 on the rule explorer and compare its repeated triangular gaps with the pyramid; inspect a smaller part of each.
rooms.observable: Rule90 grows a patterned row history; the pyramid repeats smaller corner forms in three-dimensional space.
rooms.mechanism: Explorer uses bit-table updates; SierpinskiPyramid _recursive_build divides current_size and recursively places corner children until depth0.
rooms.limit: The pyramid is built by recursion, not agents exchanging messages, and the visible likeness does not establish a working circuit or universal computer.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Expose one construction step on each artifact so visitors can match a local update with a recursive level.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified.

rooms.question: What evidence would distinguish persistent organisation from a changing picture?
rooms.ontology: A local state can be updated by neighbour averaging plus perturbation; a regime label is a hypothesis about its resulting behaviour.
rooms.action: Watch a region over several updates and describe what persists, what changes and what disappears from view.
rooms.observable: Coloured state clusters evolve under averaging and random perturbation; the visualiser samples every third cell.
rooms.mechanism: evolve_self_organization creates a next grid using neighbour average and noise; lambda interpolates coupling0.35→0 and randomness0→4. Hard-coded band0.35–0.65 supplies the regime name.
rooms.limit: This parameter is not a measurement of Langton rule-table lambda or proof that life exists only in a numerical interval. Display subsampling can hide state changes.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Add matched-seed low/mid/high parameter fields and measure a defined persistence statistic before naming a critical regime.
